sections.heading: One Window or the Whole House
body: **Replace the window that bothers you most, or every window you own.** A small job gets the same care as a whole house.
Pick the style that fits how you use each room:
list: **Casement and double hung** for the rooms you open every day
**Double sliding, center vent and end vent sliding** for wide openings
**Awning and hopper** for basements and small spaces
**Picture and bay** for the big views

sections.heading: Older Homes and Crooked Openings
body: **Old houses rarely have square openings, and we fit them anyway.** We work each new window into the frame and trim you already have, then finish the edges so the room looks clean.
That goes for upper floors and storm-damaged openings too, not just the easy ground-floor windows.

sections.quote: They managed to work new windows so quickly into our mangled up 80 year old window openings and trim, and made it look easy.
sections.name: Dustin M.

sections.heading: Fewer, Larger Windows Where They Fit
body: Older houses often have lots of small windows. When we measure, we look for openings where one larger window can take the place of two or three small ones. The house looks cleaner from the street, and you have fewer windows to buy and install, which can take a real bite out of the cost of the job.

sections.quote: Our house originally had 34 windows, and Anthony was able to make it so that we would only need 17 windows to replace the whole house.
sections.name: Rob R.

sections.heading: Cooler Rooms and Less Noise
body: **New energy efficient windows seal tight, so rooms hold the temperature you set.** The drafts stop, and most of the noise from outside goes with them.
You feel the change the first hot afternoon or the first cold night.

sections.quote: The best thing I can say is that these windows really cool down the house.

items.title: Clean-up and a walkthrough

footer.about: We're a locally owned and operated exterior remodeling company with hubs in Wichita and Oklahoma City. We replace windows, install vinyl siding and put in sliding patio doors.
why: Manufacturer's lifetime warranty on energy efficient windows
We beat a lower price on a comparable product

Your customers already make your case. You hold a 5.0 on 140 Google reviews, and they say it plainly: "Small company with owner involvement." "My house is much quieter and cooler now." "If you are looking into getting new windows call Evolve Exteriors first!"
Your website hides all of it behind sample text, and its phone buttons reach neither office.
So we built this site around their words.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Exterior Company People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page: what your site does today and what we changed.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn who you are and where you work.
problems: Every call button dials 1234567890, so a visitor who taps your Wichita number reaches nothing.
The Oklahoma City number is plain text with no button, so your second office can't be reached by tap.
The top of the page says "Best Professional Window Installation" with no town, so Google can't tell you work in Wichita.
Your 140 reviews are missing; the only quote is sample text from "Samantha Johnson".
fixes: Wichita and Oklahoma City are each one tap to call, on every page.
A headline that says exterior remodeling company in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
Real reviews from your customers, each beside the point it proves.
cards.alsoAdd: Hourly speed monitoring that keeps your site fast for visitors on phones, and speed is something Google uses to rank you.

cards.title: Window Replacement
cards.why: Windows are about three quarters of your written reviews, and they have no real page.
problems: "Our Windows" is eight style names with nothing on warranty, price or install, so Google has little to rank and shoppers little reason to call.
fixes: A full page for window replacement in Wichita, KS: styles, warranty, price match and install day.
Reviews on basement windows, old houses and cooler rooms, each beside its point.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

cards.title: Vinyl Siding
cards.why: Your crews finish siding in a day, and siding has no real page.
problems: "Vinyl Siding" opens a leftover page called "copy-of-our-windows": one siding paragraph, then window text ending mid-sentence on "that fit your."
fixes: A full page for vinyl siding in Wichita, KS, and the siding button opens it.
Your siding reviews beside the work they describe.
cards.alsoAdd: A check of what your competitors offer, so services you didn't think to mention still get their own pages.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a ready customer reaches you, at either office.
problems: "Get a Free Estimate", "Get a Quote" and "About Us" all lead back to the homepage.
The email link writes to info@mysite.com, a stranger's address.
fixes: Both numbers one tap away, with your hours and your real email.
A short list of what to have ready before you call.
cards.alsoAdd: Call and form tracking that shows which pages and towns your leads come from.

onboardingQuestions: Colton's and Riley's surnames, and how they want to be introduced on the site (the Thumbtack name "Helton" is unconfirmed).
Which phone number should lead on the site for Oklahoma City customers, and do they want the OKC number shown in the header as well as the footer and contact page?

Is there a street address to show? Only an unopened Angi snippet gives 2733 E. Kite Ct., Wichita; the Google profile shows 7804 E Funston St #208, Wichita. Which is current, and is there an OKC address?

Full list of services: entry doors, egress windows, basement windows beyond two reviews, bay and picture windows, soffit and fascia (one owner reply and a few reviews). Triple-pane windows (the blog and one review mention them)?
Window brand they install. "Wallside's Awning Windows" is the only name on the site and we could not confirm a dealer relationship, so no brand is named.
Does the manufacturer's lifetime warranty transfer to the next owner, and are the windows made in the USA? Only one review says so.
Years in business: the site says 5+ years in the industry, reviews start March 2025. What can we say?
Licensing, insurance, BBB or any certification to verify and show. None is stated anywhere we found.
Is financing through a named lender, and may we say "low-to-no interest"? The financing page also names the wrong city (Addison).
Should the 15% off sign-up offer on the current homepage be honored on the new site?
Typical install times for windows and siding, and what is included in the window, siding and patio door consultations, so the steps can be firmed up.
Logo file and brand colors (not sampled; none held in our files).
Is Evolve Egress and Exteriors (named in one review and on Angi) the same company?
